issues.description: Method name mismatch for the quantity getter: Template class de.tum.cit.ase.Stock calls StockIngredient.getQuantity(), but the template StockIngredient class only defines retrieveQuantity(). The solution and the problem statement expect a conventional getter named getQuantity(). This mismatch causes a compilation error in the provided template and prevents students from compiling and running their code.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a conventional getter public int getQuantity() to the template StockIngredient class that returns the ingredient quantity (or rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity()). This will match the calls in Stock.java and align the template with the solution and the problem statement guidance to provide getters for all private fields.

issues.description: The concept is the quantity getter for StockIngredient. The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" (problem_statement.md line 22). In the template, StockIngredient declares a method named retrieveQuantity() (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java lines 36-38), but other template code (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java lines 36-37) calls getQuantity(). The solution implementation uses getQuantity() as well (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java lines 36-38). This inconsistent identifier naming (retrieveQuantity vs getQuantity) prevents students from compiling and mapping the problem requirement to the template API.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to the conventional getter name getQuantity() (public int getQuantity()) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java so it matches calls in Stock.java and the solution, and aligns with the problem statement's expectation of standard getters.
